# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview

This two-file TypeScript change deletes the exported `RequestOptions` interface from `src/types.ts` and widens the import in `src/client.ts` to `{ RequestOptions, ClientOptions }`. The runtime behavior of `request()` (fetch with `AbortSignal.timeout(options.timeoutMs)`) is untouched.

Despite the stated intent to "preserve existing contracts," the PR does the opposite on the type level: `src/client.ts` still imports and uses `RequestOptions`, which no longer exists in `./types`, so the project no longer type-checks/compiles. The newly imported `ClientOptions` is also unused.

## Verification

Verification was disabled for this run: `pr_review_verify` (`action: list`) found no user-level `verificationBaselines` configured, so no baseline was selected or run. Note that when enabled, baselines execute PR code unsandboxed (lifecycle supervision covers only the original POSIX process group); an external sandbox/container wrapper is recommended for untrusted PRs. Findings below were instead validated by direct source inspection of `src/types.ts`, `src/client.ts`, and a repository-wide `RequestOptions` usage search.

## Findings

### [P0] Restore the `RequestOptions` export deleted from types.ts
**Severity:** P0
**Rationale:** The removed line `export interface RequestOptions { timeoutMs: number }` was the only declaration of this type. After this PR, `src/client.ts:1` imports `RequestOptions` from `"./types"` and `src/client.ts:3` uses it as the parameter type of the exported `request()` function, so TypeScript fails with `Module '"./types"' has no exported member 'RequestOptions'` (TS2305) — the project will not compile regardless of input. A repository-wide search confirms `src/client.ts` is the only consumer, so keeping the interface in `types.ts` (or moving the declaration into `client.ts` and updating the import) is required. This also silently breaks any external consumers importing this public type.
**Location:** `src/types.ts:1-1 LEFT`

### [nit] Drop the unused `ClientOptions` import in client.ts
**Severity:** nit
**Rationale:** The import was widened to `{ RequestOptions, ClientOptions }`, but `ClientOptions` is never referenced in `src/client.ts`. Remove it or use it, whichever the intended refactor calls for.
**Location:** `src/client.ts:1-1 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness

All requested lanes completed. (5/5 passes: overview, correctness, correctness-contracts, security-performance, performance-resources — all `status: complete`, no partial/failed lanes.)

## Strengths and notes

- The runtime request path (timeout via `AbortSignal.timeout`) is intentionally left unchanged, keeping behavior stable.
- **Correctness:** the only functional defect is the broken import/export contract above; `normalizeClientOptions` and `ClientOptions` remain intact.
- **Security:** no security regressions found in the changed lines.
- **Performance:** no resource or performance regressions introduced.
